nodes.name: Slurry Preparation and Tape Casting
nodes.procedure: NiO powder was mixed with xylene (solvent), ethanol (co-solvent), fish oil (dispersant), potato starch (pore-forming agent), and ZrO₂ beads in a ball mill for 24 h. Subsequently, polyalkylene glycol (PAG, dispersant), butyl benzyl phthalate (BBP, plasticizer), and polyvinyl butyral (PVB, binder) were added to the mixture, followed by another 24 h of ball milling to ensure homogeneous dispersion. The well-mixed slurry was then cast onto a carrier film using a tape-casting method, where the doctor blade position was adjusted to maintain a constant casting speed of 250 mm min⁻¹ and a blade height of 300 μm. After natural drying at room temperature, the green tapes were transferred to a cutting table and precisely cut into appropriate sizes based on the required electrode area for testing.

nodes.name: Hot Pressing
nodes.procedure: Multiple layers of the cut tapes were stacked according to the desired electrode thickness. The stacked tapes were then hot-pressed at 80°C under 10 MPa for 18 min to ensure proper lamination.

nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD analysis are performed on the TPE before and after soaking in KOH solution. As shown in Figure 2a,b, two strong characteristic peaks at 44.6° and 51.9° correspond to metallic Ni (JCPDF, Card No.04-0850). ... new diffraction peaks emerge at 19.3°, 33.1°, and 38.5°, which can be indexed to the (001), (100), and (101) planes of β-Ni(OH)₂ phase (JCPDF, Card No.14-0117)

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p3/2 peak at 855.38 eV and main peaks at 855.38/873.10 eV (spin-orbit splitting 17.72 eV) confirm Ni(OH)₂ after KOH treatment; untreated shows Ni 2p3/2 at 853.79 eV (NiO) and metallic Ni peaks (852.38/869.62 eV) which decrease.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Ni 2p spectra shows distinct changes upon KOH treatment. For the KOH-treated sample, the Ni 2p3/2 peak centers at 855.38 eV, characteristic of Ni(OH)₂.[19] The Ni 2p main peaks appear at 855.38 and 873.10 eV with a spin-orbit splitting of 17.72 eV, confirming the formation of Ni(OH)₂ phase. In contrast, the untreated sample exhibits a Ni 2p3/2 peak at 853.79 eV, typical of NiO.[20] Notably, the intensity of metallic Ni peaks (852.38 and 869.62 eV) decreases significantly after KOH treatment

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals pristine TPE with 3D porous structure of small pores (0.2-2 μm) and strip-like pores (30 μm length, 5 μm width); after KOH treatment, hierarchical structure decorated with hexagonal β-Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cross-sectional SEM image (Figure S1, Supporting Information) reveals that the TPE structure consists of a dense network of sponge-like small pores (0.2 - 2 μm in diameter) interspersed with large strip-like pores (30 μm in length and 5 μm in width) ... SEM analysis shows dramatic surface structural changes, where the initially porous TPE matrix (Figure 3a) transforms into a hierarchical structure decorated with hexagonal β-Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets after KOH treatment (Figure 3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows intimate integration of sheet-like Ni(OH)₂ nanostructures within porous Ni matrix.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image (Figure 3c) reveals an intimate integration of sheet-like Ni(OH)₂ nanostructures within the porous Ni matrix, corroborating the surface morphology observed in SEM.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows β-Ni(OH)₂ lattice spacings of 0.16 nm (110) and 0.22 nm (101) at the Ni/Ni(OH)₂ interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image (Figure 3d, Area 2) clearly resolves the crystallographic features of β-Ni(OH)₂, exhibiting characteristic lattice spacings of 0.16 nm and 0.22 nm, corresponding to the (110) and (101) crystallographic planes, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping shows uniform Ni distribution throughout matrix and concentrated O distribution coinciding with Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spatial distribution of chemical elements was mapped using EDX (Figure 3e,f), providing complementary evidence for the phase transformation. ... Notably, the oxygen mapping reveals concentrated distributions specifically coinciding with the locations of Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: MIP confirms hierarchical pore architecture with bimodal distribution: micropores at 0.3 μm and larger pores at 1.5 μm, total porosity 48%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Mercury Intrusion Porosimetry (MIP) analysis further confirms this hierarchical pore architecture (Figure S3, Supporting Information), revealing a bimodal distribution with micropores centered at 0.3 μm and larger pores at 1.5 μm, with a total porosity of 48%.
